newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says foreign share buying rules unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says foreign share buying rules unchanged.

text.p: A senior Gazprom official said on Thursday that rules governing acquisitions of the gas monopoly's shares by foreigners had not changed.
"Nothing has changed," said Eduard Ivanov, head of Gazprom's securities department. "The only way for foreigners to acquire shares is within the nine percent quota through ADRs."
In its Thursday edition the Wall Street Journal Europe quoted Gazprom Chairman Rem Vyakhirov as saying Gazprom was encouraging foreign investment in its domestic shares.
Gazprom operates a strict separation of shares available for domestic and foreign investors.
Its charter specifies that nine percent of its capital is available for investment by non-residents.

Of this nine percent Gazprom has so far issued about one percent in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADSs) -- similar to American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) --, which trade at a massive premium to the domestic shares.
In practice, non-residents can buy domestic shares through Russian registered companies, often the Russian subsidiaries of Western investment banks. Gazprom appears to have tacitly accepted this.
Ivanov said Russian subsidiaries of foreign companies could buy domestic Gazprom shares freely, but their ownership rights were still governed by the restrictions in the charter.
The Wall Street Journal said Vyakhirev's remarks in an interview appeared to be the first time the company had openly stated that foreigners can buy its domestic shares.

But Gazprom bitterly opposed a widely publicised plan by a Regent Pacific Group unit to set up a foreign-based fund investing in domestic Gazprom shares through a local subsidiary. Regent dropped the plan this week.

Vyakhirev told the Wall Street Journal that companies registered in Russia had rights equal to those of other investors, but they could not transfer the shares to outside investors. He said Regent's plan would have damaged Gazprom.
Gazprom closed sharply higher at $0.630 after $0.571 on Wednesday. Its ADSs, equivalent to 10 underlying shares, were $17.825 at 1545 GMT, down from $19.425 at Wednesday's close.
